scenes.heading: Mixed numbers and improper fractions
scenes.sub: Two ways to write more than one whole
scenes.say: What's the difference between eleven quarters and two and three quarters? Nothing! They're the same amount, written two different ways. Let's learn to switch between them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: 11 muffins in boxes of 4 = 2 full boxes and 3 left over
scenes.breaks: Muffins are whole things. Fractions can be cut into any number of equal parts.
scenes.say: A bakery packs muffins in boxes of four. Eleven muffins fill two full boxes, with three left over: three quarters of a box. So eleven quarters equals two and three quarters. The improper fraction counts every muffin. The mixed number counts full boxes first.
scenes.caption: A bakery packs muffins in boxes of 4. 11 muffins fill 2 full boxes, with 3 left over: 3/4 of a box. So 11/4 = 2¾. The improper fraction counts every muffin. The mixed number counts full boxes first.

scenes.heading: Three kinds of fraction
points: Proper: top smaller than bottom, e.g. 3/5
Improper: top equal or bigger, e.g. 7/4
scenes.say: A proper fraction has a smaller top than bottom, like three fifths, and is less than one. An improper fraction has a top that's equal or bigger, like seven quarters. A mixed number is a whole number plus a fraction, like two and three quarters.
scenes.caption: A proper fraction has a smaller top than bottom, like 3/5, and is less than 1. An improper fraction has a top that's equal or bigger, like 7/4. A mixed number is a whole number plus a fraction, like 2¾.

scenes.heading: Mixed to improper
scenes.say: To turn a mixed number into an improper fraction: times, add, keep. For three and two fifths, multiply three by five to get fifteen, add two to get seventeen, and keep the fives. Seventeen fifths.
scenes.caption: To turn a mixed number into an improper fraction: times, add, keep. For 3⅖, multiply 3 × 5 = 15, add 2 to get 17, keep the 5. 17/5.

scenes.heading: Improper to mixed
scenes.question: Write 23/6 as a mixed number.
scenes.say: Going the other way, divide. Six goes into twenty-three three times, which makes eighteen. The remainder is five. That goes on top, over the same six. So twenty-three sixths is three and five sixths.
scenes.caption: Going the other way, divide. 6 goes into 23 three times, making 18. The remainder is 5. That goes on top, over the same 6. So 23/6 = 3⅚.

scenes.heading: Simplify at the end
scenes.question: Write 30/4 as a mixed number in simplest form.
scenes.say: Thirty quarters. Four goes into thirty seven times, which is twenty-eight, remainder two. That gives seven and two quarters. Two quarters simplifies to one half, so the answer is seven and a half.
scenes.caption: 30/4. 4 goes into 30 seven times (28), remainder 2. That gives 7 2/4. 2/4 simplifies to 1/2, so the answer is 7½.

scenes.heading: Watch out
scenes.say: The most common mistakes: multiplying by the top instead of the bottom, changing the bottom number, and forgetting to add the top. The pieces don't change size, so the bottom always stays the same.

points: Improper → mixed: divide, remainder on top
scenes.say: Quick recap. Improper fractions are one or more. Mixed to improper: times, add, keep. Improper to mixed: divide, and the remainder goes on top. Always simplify the fraction part. Now try the practice questions!
